name: Tandon's
why_it_matters: Founded in 1981 in the old Patna University belt, Tandon's built a four-decade reputation on a tight, traditional menu. The kesar peda uses real saffron rather than colour, and the chandrakala (khoya pastry in syrup) is the shop's signature.
insider_tip: The chandrakala is fragile — eat in-store the same day rather than packing for travel. Laung latika sells out by mid-evening on weekends.

name: Shantilal's Sweets & Ventures
why_it_matters: A Jakkanpur sweet-and-namkeen institution near Dayanand Girls School — modernised packaging and clean storefront, but the khaja and balushahi recipes are unchanged. Now also handles catering and a small restaurant arm.
insider_tip: The rabdi rasgulla is sold from a separate counter at the back — order early in the day; the rabdi runs out before evening rush.
signature_address: Sabji Mandi, Kannulal Road, near Dayanand Girls School, Jakkanpur, Patna 800001

name: Mahavir Mandir Naivedyam Counter
why_it_matters: The temple-run prasad counter at Mahavir Mandir, opposite Patna Junction. The boondi-based naivedyam laddoo is made on temple premises by trained sevayats and sold in standard tin packs — a fixed-price, fixed-recipe sweet that doubles as a Patna takeaway gift.
insider_tip: Counter is busiest Tuesday-Saturday around the morning aarti. Buy the smaller tin if you're flying — the larger one crumbles in cabin luggage.
signature_address: Mahavir Mandir, Mahavir Mandir Road, opposite Patna Junction, Patna 800001

name: Chourasiya ji ki Purani Litti Dukan
why_it_matters: Established 1956 opposite the masjid at Pillar 6 on Station Road, this is among the oldest continuously running litti carts in central Patna. Ghee-dipped sattu litti with mustard oil chokha — the rustic version locals push tourists toward when correcting them about restaurant litti.
insider_tip: Open 11am-7pm. Cash only. The cart sets up against the wall — there is no seating; eat standing or take to the parked car.
signature_address: Station Road, New Market, opposite masjid, Pillar 6, Patna 800001

name: RK Litti Shop
why_it_matters: Operates inside Maurya Lok complex — the central market arcade off Dak Bungalow Road that locals treat as Patna's old food court. The litti rounds are coal-charred and served in a paper plate with three chokhas; the queue is the menu.
insider_tip: Lunch only (11am-8pm). Maurya Lok parking is street-side and chaotic; auto-rickshaw is faster than driving in.
signature_address: Maurya Lok Complex, near Dak Bungalow, Patna 800001
